canonical_data: per-session workspace directories with conversation files, an execution working directory, distilled experience files, and plugin definitions the user authors
current_repo_note: Archived by its maintainer with no notice on the readme or the still-live documentation site, so both surfaces still read as an active project. It was never published to a package index; the only install paths are a clone or a version-control URL against one of two tags, against a declared version far beyond them.
strengths: Code verification is real machinery rather than a prompt, walking the syntax tree with configurable allow and block lists and an explicit dangerous-builtins list, feeding a bounded revise-and-retry loop

Stateful execution is the design centre: the kernel keeps in-memory tables alive across turns, so multi-step analysis composes instead of restarting, which is the specific thing query-generating agents cannot do
Unusually broad provider coverage for its era, spanning five vendors plus local runtimes, with container execution by default and a published executor image
weaknesses: The repository is archived with no notice on the readme or the live documentation site, so both still read as active
It was never published to a package index, so it cannot be a dependency and the only install paths are a clone or a version-control URL
No approval step exists before generated code runs, which its own contribution wish-list asks for, and there is no tool-server support
why_it_matters: The clearest worked example of a data agent built on generated Python over live in-memory state rather than on generated queries, with syntax-tree verification of that code before it runs.
